pages.title: Agent Host Runtime
pages.purpose: Explains what runs inside the Agent Host utilityProcess: the in-process pi-coding-agent session manager, model runtime, skills/plugins, auth, file access, session watch/index/title, and toolchain-aware execution environment.
instructions: Focus on responsibilities and flows rather than a file inventory.

pages.title: RPC and Contract Layer
pages.purpose: Describes the typed Api/Streams contract, the MessagePort wire protocol, RPC client/server behavior, host-to-main parent RPC, main-bridged host requests, and contract coverage enforcement.
instructions: Document the five wire message kinds, lease semantics, error shaping, and the trusted-request boundary.

pages.title: Security Model
pages.purpose: Cross-cutting security: renderer sandbox/CSP, preload location/message policies, trusted IPC sender checks, credential vaults, secret redaction, browser isolation, protocol/certificate handling, and updater trust.
instructions: State security invariants only where source establishes them; note best-effort protections explicitly.

pages.title: Three-Process Architecture
pages.purpose: Explains the Electron main / Agent Host utilityProcess / Renderer model, how the processes connect (MessagePort, preload bridge, parentPort), Host supervision and restart, and the no-internal-server principle.
instructions: Cite entrypoints and lifecycle wiring. Do not claim guarantees the code does not establish.

pages.title: Development and Verification Guide
pages.purpose: Change guide for developing and verifying the app: dev/build scripts, the verify gate, test runner, contract/security checks, packaging, CI workflows, and release build scripts.
instructions: Ground commands in package.json scripts and script source; the verify sequence is authoritative for pre-commit expectations.

pages.title: Windows Managed Process Helper Guide
pages.purpose: Focused change guide for the Windows x64 Rust helper and Job Object containment: helper responsibilities, JSON frame protocol, build/reproducibility pipeline, integrity verification, and the acceptance tests that gate it.
instructions: Explain build IDs, provenance, fail-closed checks, and where the helper path/integrity is validated.

pages.title: Builtin Browser
pages.purpose: Explains the Main-owned WebContentsView browser: tabs and profiles, network policy and isolation, Agent authorization/lease flow, capability runtime, advanced browser mode, header rules, CDP, downloads, snippets, tab restore.
instructions: Explain the user/agent control boundary and where authorization happens before tool side effects.

pages.title: Desktop Shell and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Covers the Electron main shell: window creation and state, menus, tray and badges, single-instance lock, deep links, update manager/adapter, notifications, diagnostics export, crash recovery, and app:// protocol serving.
instructions: Describe update phases and trust boundaries; note platform-specific differences only where source establishes them.

pages.title: Managed Background Processes
pages.purpose: Describes process_* tools, the ManagedProcessService state machine, POSIX process-group backend and Windows Job Object helper backends, crash reaper/journal, policy/limits, output buffering and cursors, readiness and capability gating.
instructions: Document limits, fail-closed behavior, and the reaper journal path.

pages.title: Messaging Channels (WeChat, Telegram, Feishu/Lark)
pages.purpose: Explains the channel framework: ChannelManager lifecycle, adapters for weixin/telegram/feishu, inbound policy, pairing and bindings, lane scheduling, Pi-session bridging, media handling, credentials, and outbound rendering.
instructions: Describe outbound-only transport where source establishes it; note unsupported/partial behaviors.

pages.title: Sessions and Project Files
pages.purpose: Describes session lifecycle and storage under ~/.pi/agent, session indexing/watching/titles, file listing/reading/download/preview, file watching, search, git status and worktrees.
instructions: Cite persistence paths and on-disk change flow.

pages.title: Toolchain Management
pages.purpose: Explains developer tool discovery and management: ToolchainManager scanning, discovery registry, probes, bundled core tools, managed component catalog/installer, project detection, resolution, execution contexts and environment construction.
instructions: Explain snapshot/revision flow from main to host and the resolution cache.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical onboarding: what Pi Agent Desktop is, system requirements, install/dev setup, first run, configuration, key commands, and navigation to the rest of the wiki.
instructions: Ground every non-obvious claim in source; the README describes intent, source defines behavior.
